features.name: Academic attainment
features.description: Captures the level of formal technical education or academic credential the letter presents.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical background only.
Master's degree in computer science or a related technical field.
Doctoral degree in computer science or a related technical field.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures hands-on design or ownership of agent-based systems, especially with explicit guardrails, control planes, or bounded autonomy.

levels.descriptor: No agentic systems experience is mentioned.
References agents in passing without clear ownership or design detail.
Describes a concrete agentic pipeline or tooling example.
Shows end-to-end ownership of agentic architecture, including boundaries, supervision, permissions, logging, or auditability.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures practical command of data structures and algorithms shown through concrete engineering examples.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.name: Applied AI production maturity
features.description: Captures whether the applicant has shipped AI or LLM systems in production and understands reliability, evaluation, and operational hardening.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Collaboration and learning mindset
features.description: Captures openness to learning and a collaborative stance toward security specialists or internal users of the tooling.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention collaboration with security partners.
Implies support for other engineers, but not specifically partnership with security specialists.
Explicitly states readiness to work with security engineers or build for their workflows.
Shows explicit partnership mindset plus concrete evidence of learning from, serving, or collaborating with security specialists.

features.name: Developer enablement orientation
features.description: Captures whether the applicant frames security tooling as helping developers adopt safer defaults with less friction.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how much the letter substantiates claims with concrete examples, mechanisms, architecture details, or named work.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on generic claims, requirement-matching language, or buzzwords.
Mixes broad claims with a few specifics, leaving important claims under-evidenced.
Backs most major claims with concrete examples, mechanisms, or outcomes.
Is densely specific enough that the reader can clearly picture what the applicant built and why it mattered.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures how central and production-grade Go appears in the applicant's backend engineering experience.

levels.descriptor: Go is mentioned but not shown as a central working language.
Go is described as primary, daily, or most-used.
Go is tied to clear backend or infrastructure ownership.
Go is central to concrete role-matching systems design, especially security or agent infrastructure.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter states the concrete outcomes or effects of the applicant's work.

levels.descriptor: Mostly lists interests or responsibilities with no clear outcomes.
Provides background counts but little evidence of what changed because of the work.
Shows at least one clear result or before-and-after effect.
Shows concrete, vivid, or measured outcomes that make the applicant's contribution easy to evaluate.

features.name: Maintainability and rigor mindset
features.description: Captures whether the applicant emphasizes reliability, operability, careful boundaries, maintenance, testing, and long-term system care.

levels.descriptor: Shows no explicit maintainability or reliability orientation.
Implies care for quality but not as a recurring theme.
Clearly values maintainable, dependable systems or draws on maintenance experience.
Makes long-term operability a central lens, emphasizing inheritance, quiet resilience, or higher standards for security-critical software.

features.name: Narrative quality
features.description: Captures whether the letter presents a coherent, memorable, well-shaped story or voice rather than a generic checklist.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like an interchangeable template or a flat list of qualifications.
The letter is competent but generic, with limited individuality in framing or voice.
The letter has a distinctive opening, viewpoint, or sustained framing device.
The letter is memorable and cohesive, with a clear throughline linking the opening idea, past work, and motivation for this role.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Captures ongoing attacker-minded practice outside ordinary development work, especially through CTFs or similar exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional or casual CTF participation or similar practice.
The letter shows regular CTF participation or sustained offensive practice.
The letter shows strong competitive results or especially serious, ongoing offensive-security practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures responsibility for public or upstream codebases, including contribution, maintenance, releases, or fixing dependencies at the source.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or maintenance described.
Mentions occasional upstream patches or light contribution.
Shows active contribution or maintenance with review or release responsibility.
Maintains a used project or framework with sustained community, release, review, or user-support responsibilities.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition, seriousness, and follow-through of self-directed projects outside formal work.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures motivation for foundational infrastructure work whose impact compounds across many teams or products.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention foundational leverage or broader organizational impact.
Expresses a general desire for scale or impact but without a clear platform orientation.
Explicitly wants infrastructure or foundational work that benefits many teams.
Repeatedly frames motivation around downstream leverage, central-platform responsibility, or quiet improvements inherited across an organization.

features.name: Production delivery scope
features.description: Captures the breadth and depth of concrete production-system ownership, including launches, maintenance, testing, and operated services.

levels.descriptor: Describes launching or owning only a small number of production services, such as 2.
Describes a moderate shipped footprint, such as about 4 production services.
Describes repeated launch and maintenance experience across many services, such as 6 or more.

features.name: Professional software tenure
features.description: Captures the amount of directly relevant full-time software-engineering experience the applicant claims.

levels.descriptor: Below the role minimum or unclear on relevant experience length.
Roughly meets the minimum, around 2 to 3 years of relevant experience.
Shows solid mid-level experience, around 4 to 5 years.
Shows strong experience depth, around 6 or more years.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how central and production-grade Python appears in the applicant's services, tooling, automation, or agent work.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or only minimally mentioned.
Python is mentioned for light scripting or general familiarity.
Python is used regularly for tooling, automation, analysis, or services.
Python is presented as production-grade and central, with evidence of robust service or tooling development.

features.name: Requirement mapping
features.description: Captures how explicitly the letter maps the applicant's background to the posting's stated qualifications, responsibilities, or exact role target.

levels.descriptor: Makes little direct connection to the posting beyond naming the role.
Mentions some relevant qualifications, but the mapping to the posting is mostly implicit.
Clearly addresses several core requirements or responsibilities from the posting.
Systematically maps experience to the posting, with explicit coverage of the main requirements and responsibilities.

features.name: Role-specific motivation
features.description: Captures how specifically and compellingly the letter explains why this exact role or mission fits the applicant's motivations.

levels.descriptor: Shows generic interest in the company or job title with little role-specific reasoning.
Shows some relevant interest, but the motivation remains broad or interchangeable.
Clearly ties motivation to security engineering, developer enablement, or backend tooling.
Gives nuanced and convincing motivation tightly tied to this team's charter and responsibilities.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience reviewing systems for security weaknesses and validating remediation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security automation framing
features.description: Captures how well the letter understands the role as scaling security work through tooling, workflow design, and automation rather than generic software development.

levels.descriptor: Does not explicitly frame security work as an automation or systems problem.
Mentions automation as useful but without a strong view of what it scales.
Clearly frames automation as a way to reduce manual security workload or extend team reach.
Shows nuanced understanding of the role as scaling scarce security expertise through systems such as triage, structured response, or variant analysis.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: Captures the rigor and relevance of formal third-party security certifications or credential signals.

levels.descriptor: No security credential is mentioned.
Mentions a baseline credential such as Security+ or equivalent fundamentals.
Mentions a demanding practical credential such as OSCP or equivalent.

features.name: Security engineering philosophy
features.description: Captures whether the letter articulates a thoughtful view of what good security engineering is for and how it should be practiced.

levels.descriptor: No real security viewpoint is articulated beyond general interest.
The letter states that security matters, but the philosophy is thin or generic.
The letter presents a clear viewpoint, such as proactive assistance, quiet resilience, or defaults over policy.
The letter offers a nuanced security philosophy that is clearly tied to the applicant's engineering choices and the role's mission.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Captures direct experience building tooling that automates vulnerability-report intake, classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or handling.

levels.descriptor: No past vulnerability-handling automation is mentioned.
The letter expresses interest in this problem, but gives no concrete example of having automated it.
A concrete example of triage, intake, routing, or report-handling automation is described.
The letter shows strong end-to-end automation of vulnerability handling, with clear workflow transformation or operational value.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures proofreading, grammar, spelling, and sentence-level professionalism.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors repeatedly interrupt reading or seriously undermine credibility.
Noticeable proofreading problems distract the reader more than once.
Contains some typos, but the letter remains easy to follow.
Mostly clean, with at most a minor slip.
Polished and effectively error-free at a professional standard.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures dimensions that do not clearly share an underlying construct with the recurring criteria above.

levels.descriptor: Only Go is mentioned, or language breadth is unclear.
Shows Go plus one or two additional languages.
Shows Go plus several additional languages.
Shows Go plus broad multi-language experience across many systems.
